question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Apple)

calls.reasoning: Apple guided Sep-quarter FY26 revenue +9-11% YoY on $102.47B, i.e. $111.7-113.7B, citing 2.5pt FX headwind and sharply increased supply constraints (iPhone guided mid-teens). Consensus $113.4B (MarketBeat) to $115.3B. Recent quarters landed at or above the top of guidance (from memory: Dec-25 ~16% vs 10-12%, Mar-26 ~16.6% vs 13-16%), but supply limits cap the upside this time. Median ~$114.0B, just above the top of guidance. Markets: no Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold total-revenue contract found; Polymarket has EPS-beat and segment-revenue markets and Kalshi has mention markets, none of which match these resolution terms, so no market anchor.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off Apple's Q4 FY2026 (Sep quarter, ending ~Sep 26 2026) total net sales in the Nov 2, 2026 after-close 8-K press release (initial figure; later revisions don't count). Event window: quarter already ended; only the reported number remains; resolution Nov 2, 2026 (as of Oct 21, ~12 days left).
- Year-ago quarter (Q4 FY25) revenue: $102.466B (question background).
- Q3 FY26 (Jun quarter) revenue $109.4B, +16% YoY, beat consensus ~$108.7-108.9B (digitalapplied, Aug 2026).
- Apple's Sep-quarter guidance (Jul 30, 2026 call): total revenue +9-11% YoY, implying ~$111.69B-$113.74B (AppleInsider, Oct 6 2026); this was below the ~12% analysts had modeled. iPhone guided to mid-teens % YoY growth. 2.5pt sequential FX headwind. Supply constraints on iPhone/Mac/iPad (advanced-node SoC availability) expected to 'increase significantly'. Gross margin guided 47-48%.
- Q3 Services +12% YoY, slightly below the ~$31.2B estimate.
- Consensus: MarketBeat $113.37B (EPS $1.99, +10.6% YoY); another source ~$115.3B (EPS $2.02); chartmill quotes $108.74B with a range of $102.91B-$114.58B (may be stale).
- From memory, not verified this run: recent Apple quarters came in at or above the top of the guided range (Dec-25 qtr ~16% vs 10-12% guided; Mar-26 qtr ~16.6% vs ~13-16%; Sep-25 qtr ~8% vs mid-to-high single digits).
- Context: new CEO John Ternus since Sep 1 2026, so this is his first call; HomeView launched Oct 13 and an Oct 28 Mac event, neither of which affects the Sep quarter; Qualcomm noted falling Apple revenue (its own modem share loss, not an Apple demand signal).
- Upside case: demand 'far exceeded expectations' and Apple has a habit of beating the top of guidance. Downside case: supply caps, FX, and guidance set below consensus.
- Market check: no total-revenue prediction market found for this quarter; Polymarket EPS-beat and segment markets exist but do not match these terms.
- Searched for but not found: exact Q3 FY26 guidance range vs actual; pre-release leaks; IDC/Counterpoint Sep-quarter iPhone shipment data.

calls.reasoning: Guide +9-11% YoY on $102.466B => $111.7-113.7B; consensus ~$113.4B. Apple has recently landed at or above the top of its guide (4 of 5 quarters), with one slight miss at the bottom (Q4 FY25 7.9% vs 8-10%). This quarter it explicitly flagged heavier supply constraints, a 2.5pp FX headwind and only 1-2 weeks of iPhone 18 Pro sales, which favors landing near the top of the guide rather than a big beat. Median ~$114.0B; ~11% below $112B; ~3% above $118B. No Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold/bookmaker market found by any run, so there is no crowd anchor.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the guidance ($111.7-113.7B), the year-ago base and the beat history; their medians were within $0.2B of each other. Factual dispute over consensus ($108.7B-$115.3B): the $113.37B figure from two dated Oct-2026 sources is the best-supported; $108.7B looks stale. Run 1's memory-based beat history matched Runs 2 and 3's sourced figures, so I treated it as settled. The main judgment dispute was the probability of landing below $112B (9-15%): Apple has fallen short of its guided range in only 1 of 5 quarters, and by only 0.1pp; the October iPhone order-cut reports mostly concern a period after the quarter ended. I set 11%. No web access this run, so no new retrieval.
